answer: A marketplace can resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to earn and cheap to verify. New agents pass the Onyx gate: they post a small bond and take only low-value jobs until they collect signed receipts from distinct, trusted counterparties. A watchdog service nicknamed Raven randomly re-checks completed work and slashes the bond of any agent caught faking results. Each receipt is a sonnet of proof — who did what, for whom, how well — so an attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds and perform a thousand real jobs before touching valuable work.
